extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, IP statisticians, patent office staff, researchers and users of WIPO patent statistics
extracted.subtask_description: Methodological rules and definitions WIPO uses to count, classify and present patent applications, grants, patent families, technology fields and inventor gender in the World Intellectual Property Indicators report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of a patent application (determination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The origin of a patent application is determined by the residence of the first named applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent filing activity by origin includes resident applications and applications filed abroad. For counts presented as 'by origin', the first-named applicant's residence is used to assign origin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute count vs equivalent count — applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For an absolute count, applications filed at regional offices are counted once, rather than being considered equivalent to multiple applications in the respective member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using absolute counts, a single regional filing is treated as one application. By contrast, 'equivalent' counts (see separate entry) treat regional office filings as equivalent to multiple national filings in the member states; users should consult the glossary/definitions for the formal definition of an equivalent application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent applications (definition / handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications filed at regional offices are considered equivalent to multiple applications in the relevant member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent application counts consider the regional filing as representing separate national filings across member states (i.e., one regional filing may be counted as multiple equivalent applications). See the glossary for the formal definition of equivalent application and when equivalent counts are used in tables/figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin assignment and counting for patent grants
rubrics_metrics.description: For an absolute count, patent grants issued by regional offices are counted once, rather than being considered equivalent to multiple grants in the respective member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with applications, grant counts may be presented as absolute or equivalent; absolute grant counts treat regional office grants as a single grant, whereas equivalent grant counts apportion or multiply regional grants across member states. Users should observe which counting convention (absolute/equivalent) a table or chart uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent family definition (what links a family)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families are defined as patent applications interlinked by one or more of the following: priority claim, Patent Cooperation Treaty national phase entry, continuation, continuation-in-part, internal priority, and addition or division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications. The listed linkage types are used to group related applications into families; consult EPO PATSTAT and WIPO sources for implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign-oriented patent family (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A foreign-oriented patent family includes only patent families that have at least one filing office different from the office of the applicant’s country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some foreign-oriented families include only one filing office because applicants may choose to file directly with a foreign office (example: a Canadian applicant filing directly with the USPTO forms a foreign-oriented family). Use this definition when calculating 'foreign-oriented' family totals and shares.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of utility model applications from patent family counts
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent families here include only those families associated with patent applications for inventions and exclude those associated with utility model applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing patent families in this report, utility model–related families are not counted; this affects comparability if other datasets include utility models.

rubrics_metrics.name: IPC → technology field mapping (IPC technology concordance)
rubrics_metrics.description: WIPO’s International Patent Classification (IPC) technology concordance table was used to convert IPC symbols into 35 corresponding fields of technology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence). Users should be aware of classification limitations and consult the electronic IPC technology concordance table (www.wipo.int/ipstats) for mapping details and any potential classification ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data refer to published patent applications (publication lag)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data refer to published patent applications. There is a minimum delay of 18 months between the application date and the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published-application datasets exclude very recent filings that have not yet reached the publication stage; analyses based on published applications should account for the 18-month publication lag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and capture limitations for specific technology subsets (energy technologies)
rubrics_metrics.description: For definitions of the technologies – fuel cell, geothermal, solar, wind and hydro energy – see annex A. The correspondence between IPC symbols and technology fields is not always apparent (there is no one-to-one correspondence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: IPC-based definitions are likely to capture the vast majority of patent applications in these areas, but it is difficult to capture all patents in a specific technology field. Users should consult annex A and be cautious about completeness when focusing on narrowly defined technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender attribution methodology for inventors
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to attribute gender to inventors’ names recorded in PCT applications, WIPO produced a world gender–name dictionary based on information from 13 different public sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gender is attributed to a given name on a country-by-country basis, because certain names may be considered male in one country but female in another. Users should note this probabilistic/cultural attribution approach and the underlying data sources when interpreting gender-related indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for top-20 origins and offices shown in figures/tables
rubrics_metrics.description: The top 20 offices and origins are selected based on available 2022 data, broken down by country of origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other charts apply additional inclusion thresholds. Example: for resident patent applications per USD 100 billion GDP, the top 20 origins were included if they had a GDP greater than USD 25 billion PPP and more than 100 resident patent applications. For resident patent applications per million population, the top 20 origins were included if they had a population greater than 5 million and more than 100 resident patent applications. Users should check figure notes for the exact inclusion thresholds.
